newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks up after Fed rate hike.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks up after Fed rate hike.

text.p: U.S. stocks rose on Tuesday after the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee, as widely expected, raised its target for its short-term Federal Funds rate 0.25 percentage point to 5.50 percent and left the discount rate unchanged.
The following are analysts' reaction to the move.
PHILIP ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT VALUE LINE ASSET MANAGEMENT:
-- "It's as expected. I think this means we ought to see a relief rally in both bonds and stocks over the course of the next few days.
-- "The bond market has already priced this tightening in and equities corrected some 300 points in anticipation."
-- "It's our belief this is the first of three 25 basis-point tightenings unless we see material slowing of economic activity."
JOHN WILLIAMS, MANAGING DIRECTOR AND CHIEF GLOBAL MARKETS ECONOMIST AT BANKERS TRUST
-- "The Fed finally moved so they're now officially in a tightening mode. And they will keep tightening until the economy finally slows."

-- "No one really knows the precise sensitivity of the economy to interest rates so once they're in a tightening mode, they will keep tightening until the economy slows. When that is is really not knowable. It's a late move. But better late than never."
DAVID JONES, VICE CHAIRMAN AND CHIEF ECONOMIST AT AUBREY G. LANSTOLN & CO. INC
-- "It implies that the Fed is prepared to tighten further if necesary to cool the economy off to a more sustainable and less inflationary pace."

-- "I'm still guessing that they'll do a total of a 3/4 point move, raising the Federal funds rate to six percent by the end of August from 5-1/4 percent where it stood before today's move. Probably one of those moves will be accompanied by a discount rate hike."
The Dow industrials initially jumped to a session peak, up 47 points after the rate rise. They later gave back the gains and were off nine points at 6896. The Nasdaq composite rose four to 1247.
